{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Charles Elbaum''' (May 15, 1926 – March 4, 2018) was an American physicist.

Charles Elbaum was born in [[Lublin]], Poland to parents Chil and Hannah Elbaum.<ref>{{cite news|title=Charles Elbaum|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/providence/obituary.aspx?pid=188365228|access-date=March 8, 2018|work=Providence Journal|date=March 6, 2018}}</ref> After [[World War II]], he moved to Belgium and Paris before earning a master's and doctorate from the [[University of Toronto]].

In 1959, Elbaum began teaching at [[Brown University]] as an assistant professor of [[applied physics]]. Later, he was granted fellowship in the [[American Physical Society]]. Elbaum chaired the department of physics between 1980 and 1986, and was named the Hazard Professor of Physics in 1991. Along with colleague [[Leon Cooper]], he founded the tech company ''Nestor'', dedicated to finding commercial applications for [[neural networks]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Johnson |first1=Colin |date=October 17, 1988 |title=Neural Network Startups Proliferate Across The U.S. |url=https://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/9841/title/Neural-Network-Startups-Proliferate-Across-The-U-S-/ |journal=The Scientist |volume=2 |issue=19 |access-date=March 8, 2018 }}</ref> He retired in 2001, staying on as a research professor.<ref>{{cite news|title=Remembering Charles Elbaum, Professor Emeritus of Physics|url=https://www.brown.edu/academics/physics/news/2018/03/remembering-charles-elbaum-professor-emeritus-physics|access-date=March 8, 2018|publisher=Brown University|date=March 2018}}</ref>
